subject: Pricing follow-up: burst usage, quota increases & overage terms
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finlytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-14T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Quick follow-up + numbers on burst / overage — FinLytics call recap

Hi Olivia — thanks again for taking time earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can scope a proposal that fits your usage pattern.

Call summary (high-level):
- Primary workload: interactive analytics assistant embedded in FinLytics web UI (short prompts, many sessions)
- Expected baseline daily tokens: 8M–12M tokens/day (NLU + context)
- Peak/burst behavior: up to ~80M tokens/day on earnings days (spikes lasting 2–6 hours)
- Latency requirement: 200–400ms p95 generator latency

Follow-ups we promised:
1) Provide a simple pricing worksheet showing per-1M-token unit economics at the recommended model tiers and a worked example for baseline + burst.
2) Clarify burst/quota increase mechanics and overage rates (how redwood bills spikes that exceed reserved quota).
3) Flag procurement items (MSA, SOC2 attestation, SCCs) for your legal team.

Quick asks from your side: can you confirm the target $/1M-tokens budget band you referenced on the call (you said "roughly mid-four digits" — is that $2,500–$4,500 / 1M tokens?) and whether you need hard daily caps vs. flexible quota?

Attached I’m sending: pricing_workbook (tabbed: baseline, burst model, worked example), plus a short PDF that summarizes our standard burst/overage terms. High-level preview below.

Burst & overage preview (TL;DR):
- Reserved quota is priced at committed monthly quantity with tiered unit pricing (example attached).
- Short spikes above quota are allowed (burst) and billed at an overage unit price for the incremental tokens. We offer a 48-hour smoothing window for billing anomalies on earnings days so short spikes don’t cause invoice surprises.
- For recurring spikes, we recommend a temporary quota increase (pro-rated) or moving to a larger reserved band; we’ll model costs in the workbook.

I’ll wait for your confirmation on the budget target and whether procurement prefers a hard cap on billing. If you’re comfortable, I can put together a draft canary pricing plan that holds the unit price for the first 90 days while we monitor actual usage.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Karthik Iyer
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2026-02-14_FinLytics_pricing_workbook.xlsx (xlsx), Redwood_Burst_Overage_Terms_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finlytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finlytics.com
Date: 2026-02-15T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + numbers on burst / overage — FinLytics call recap

Hi Karthik — thanks, that summary is spot on. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Budget band: Sorry for the fuzzy phrasing on the call — our finance lead gave guidance of $3,000–$4,000 per 1M tokens as our target on pilot (US pricing). We can consider higher-unit pricing if reserved commitment reduces overall monthly cost for our typical month.

2) Caps vs flexible billing: procurement prefers a soft cap with notifications rather than a hard block. We want to avoid customer impact for 1–2 hour surges but also want to avoid runaway invoices. If you can set emailed alerts at 70/90/100% of reserved quota and provide an automatic throttling option we can enable if costs spike, that would be ideal.

3) Peak characteristics: Confirming spikes are 2–6 hours, and usually 2–3x baseline on weekday earnings. We have 3 teams feeding requests but intend to throttle non-critical background jobs during peaks.

Next steps: please send the worked pricing example for baseline + a modeled cost of two earnings-day spikes per month (80M token day). Also please include the overage unit price numbers and any discounting thresholds for annual commitments. Procurement is copied — they may ask for an initial SOW and MSA redlines.

Cheers,
Olivia
Olivia Chen
Head of Product, FinLytics
olivia.chen@finlytics.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finlytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-15T13:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + numbers on burst / overage — FinLytics call recap

Thanks for the clear guidance, Olivia. I updated the pricing workbook and attached a short summary PDF with explicit unit prices for the scenarios you asked for. Summary of key numbers (all USD):

- Baseline reserved band (50M tokens/day commit): $3,200 / 1M tokens (effective blended price at that band in workbook)
- Overage (short burst) unit price: $4,500 / 1M tokens for incremental tokens beyond reserved quota
- Burst smoothing: first 48 hours of anomalous spikes are eligible for manual review; if spike is isolated we can apply an invoice adjustment credit (one-time, discretionary)
- Auto-alerting: we can provision email alerts at 70/90/100% thresholds and include an API webhook for your ops team to trigger soft-throttle logic.
- Temporary quota increases: pro-rated daily pricing for the additional reserved quantity; we can implement same-day quota increases if signed PO is in place — otherwise overage pricing applies.

Modeled example (attached workbook):
- Normal month (baseline 8M tokens/day): monthly cost estimate shown in tab "Baseline example"
- Earnings-day scenario (two days at 80M tokens): incremental overage for those 2 days billed at $4,500/1M for the difference after smoothing window. Workbook shows blended monthly impact.

I also included two optional proposals:
A) Pilot: 3-month reserved at lower commit (30M tokens/day) with capped overage cap ($75k/month) and unit price guarantee for pilot term.
B) Enterprise: 12-month reserved with stepped tiers and annual true-up — better unit economics if you predict sustained spikes.

Marissa — looped you in because FinLytics asked for MSA/SOC2 attachments for procurement. Can you share the standard MSA + SOC2 pointer and confirm the billing contact info?

Olivia — if that looks in line with your expectations I’ll prepare a one-page proposal and a sample PO template for procurement.

Best,
Karthik
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2026-02-14_FinLytics_pricing_workbook.xlsx (updated), Redwood_Burst_Overage_Terms_v1.pdf

Hi procurement team — thanks for looping in. Attaching the redlined MSA template and the SOC2 summary link: https://redwood.com/security/soc2-summary.

A few operational notes for your legal/procurement:
- Billing contact (for PO/invoice): billing@redwood.ai
- Net terms: standard 30 days; can discuss Net 45 for enterprise if required.
- Invoice adjustments: we include a one-time review window for anomalous charges flagged within 60 days. Overage credits are discretionary and applied case-by-case during pilot.

Olivia / Karthik — tagging you: we included a draft clause in the MSA (Section 4.3) that describes burst/overage smoothing and notification obligations. Please let us know if procurement prefers a hard cap clause instead of smoothing-based credits.
